name: Maluk
title: Levites and Covenant Sealers
summary: Maluk is a name that appears several times in the Old Testament, particularly in connection with the return from exile in Babylon. He is best known as one of the Levites and priests who sealed the covenant with God under Nehemiah's leadership, and as part of the genealogies in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah.

keyEvents.title: Listed in the Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Maluk is mentioned among the priests who returned from exile in Babylon to Jerusalem, as part of those who rebuilt the Jewish community.

keyEvents.title: Sealing of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Maluk was among the Levites and leaders who sealed the covenant to follow God's law during Nehemiah's time, committing themselves to faithfulness toward the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Listed Among the Descendants of Bani
keyEvents.description: A Malluk is mentioned among the descendants of Bani who had taken foreign wives and were required to send them away during Ezra's reform.

keyEvents.title: Levitical lineage
keyEvents.description: Malluk appears in the genealogies in 1 Chronicles as part of the Levitical line, confirming his place in temple service.

keyEvents.title: Priestly service after the exile
keyEvents.description: Malluk is mentioned among the priestly families who served in the temple after the rebuilding of Jerusalem and helped restore religious order.
